summary: Corrected scheduler fixed-window starvation with a bounded rotating scan over immutable insertion positions and a high-water bound per sweep. Later free-workspace runs and abandoned leases are now reached without moving rows by updated_at or replaying terminal history.

changes: RunCollection.scanActive reads at most one bounded active page in SQLite rowid/PostgreSQL pos order, keeping a captured through position until the sweep ends. Updates retain position; deletion of the previous page tail does not invalidate continuation; newly inserted rows join a later sweep.

VisuaService stores a private scan cursor and advances it only after a page is successfully processed. Existing heartbeat, workspace-lock claim, fencing, local/durable concurrency, cancellation and shutdown code is retained.

Persistent regression seeds 266 active records including eight blocked workspace queues, then verifies a later eligible run starts and later abandoned work fails within two reconciliations. A second regression exercises timestamp movement, deletion of the cursor row, terminal state change, newly inserted work and wraparound.

limits: No PostgreSQL runtime, full test suite, typecheck, build, browser/server, live database, provider, git, deployment or delegation was run; lead owns the final integrated gate.

Application scan work is bounded to 256 returned active rows per scheduler tick (the internal collection API caps requested pages at 1024). PostgreSQL pos is not indexed in existing migrations: query execution may scan/sort historical rows even though result hydration and per-tick processing are bounded. Lead explicitly retained migration/index evaluation for the combined PostgreSQL gate.

A run that becomes eligible or expires after its page was processed can wait until the next sweep. The cursor and captured high-water bound ensure updates and continuous new appends do not reset or indefinitely extend the current sweep.
The original independent review and reproduction artifacts were preserved without modification; this is a subsequent implementation and self-check.
